segments.he: שְׁחָטוֹ וְנוֹדַע וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: אָשָׁם שֶׁנִּיתַּק לִרְעִיָּה, וּשְׁחָטוֹ סְתָם — כָּשֵׁר לָעוֹלָה. אַלְמָא קָסָבַר: לָא בָּעֵי עֲקִירָה.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna that if «one slaughtered» the Paschal lamb «and it became known» afterward that the owners had died, he is exempt from bringing a sin-offering. «Rav Huna said that Rav said:» Regarding «a guilt-offering that was consigned to grazing:» If the owner of a guilt-offering dies or achieves atonement through a different guilt-offering, the animal is sent out to graze in the field until it develops a blemish, at which point it can be sold. The money from the sale is used to purchase a burnt-offering. «And» if, before it developed a blemish, someone «slaughtered it without specifying» its purpose, «it is valid as a burnt-offering.» The Gemara concludes that Rav «apparently holds that it does not require uprooting.» There is no need for an explicit declaration in order to change the status of the offering; even if it is slaughtered without its purpose specified it is valid.
